source: Kreidberg et al. (2018), AJ 156, 17, 'Global climate and atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-103b from HST and Spitzer phase curve observations' (arXiv:1805.00029). Spitzer IRAC channel 1 (3.6 um; SPIDERMAN band 3.15 to 3.95 um) phase curve. The map is the paper's degree-2 spherical-harmonic temperature map fitted with SPIDERMAN (section 3.2; thermal=True, la0 = lo0 = 0, the fourth coefficient held at 0), the model its table of model comparisons ranks best for these data. Its coefficients are read from the authors' repository at commit 425f2e8fe694760266398257a71eaa991ab322fd (github.com/lkreidberg/2017_wasp103), Figures/Ch1_best_fits/2018-02-07_14:28-spherical/results.txt (Best Parameters, named by WA103bo11-initvals.txt), the run the paper's figure scripts load (Figures/fig5_phase_curves.py, fig15_gcm_comparison.py); the paper prints no coefficients. Evaluated by SPIDERMAN, the map's coldest and hottest points give back the table's T_min and T_max; its hemisphere means come out about 100 K from the table's day and night means, whose averaging the paper does not state.
